anchors.claim_quote:
## Statement

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice
([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Let $m,\hbar>0$, put
$c:=\hbar^{2}/(2m)$, let $\mathcal F_{2}$ be the unitary Plancherel transform of
[[thm-nrqm-composites-real-multipliers-and-free-bounded-potential-operators]]
clause (b) in dimension $d=3$, let $V:\mathbb R^{3}\to\mathbb R$ be measurable
and put $W:=V/c$. For a measurable $U$ let $M_U$ be the maximal
multiplication operator on $L^2(\mathbb R^3;\mathbb C)$, with
$D(M_U):=\{f\in L^2:Uf\in L^2\}$ and $M_Uf:=Uf$. Write
$$A_{0}:=\mathcal F_{2}^{*}M_{4\pi^{2}|\xi|^{2}}\mathcal F_{2},\qquad D(A_{0}):=\bigl\{f\in L^{2}(\mathbb R^{3};\mathbb C):|\xi|^{2}\mathcal F_{2}f\in L^{2}(\mathbb R^{3};\mathbb C)\bigr\},$$
$$A:=A_{0}+M_{W},\quad D(A):=D(A_{0}),\qquad H_{0}:=cA_{0},\qquad H:=cA=cA_{0}+M_{V}.$$
$D(A_{0})\subseteq D(M_V)=D(M_W)$ is assumed, and assume that
$A=A_0+M_W$ is self-adjoint on $D(A_0)$. These two hypotheses hold
automatically for real bounded measurable $V$ by
[[thm-nrqm-composites-real-multipliers-and-free-bounded-potential-operators]]
clauses (a),(c), so every original bounded-potential case is retained.
So $A_{0}$ is the operator $-\Delta_{w}$ of
[[lem-nrqm-central-free-operator-differential-identification]] and
$D(A_{0})=W^{2,2}(\mathbb R^{3};\mathbb C)$
([[def-sobolev-space-wkp-and-its-norm]]). For a self-adjoint operator $T$ write
$E_{T}$ for the regular projection valued measure of
[[thm-spectral-theorem-for-unbounded-self-adjoint-operators]] and
$\mu^{T}_{\psi}(B):=\langle E_{T}(B)\psi,\psi\rangle$ for $\psi\in L^{2}$. Then:

(a) $A$ and $H$ are self-adjoint with domain $D(A)=W^{2,2}(\mathbb R^{3};\mathbb C)$,
and $H=cA$ and $H_{0}=cA_{0}$ hold as operator identities on that common domain;

(b) for every Borel set $B\subseteq\mathbb R$,
$$E_{H}(cB)=E_{A}(B),\qquad E_{H_{0}}(cB)=E_{A_{0}}(B);$$
consequently $\mu^{H}_{\psi}(cB)=\mu^{A}_{\psi}(B)$ for every $\psi$ and every
Borel $B$, and $\sigma(H)=c\,\sigma(A)$, $\sigma(H_{0})=c\,\sigma(A_{0})$;

(c) for every $t\in\mathbb R$, with $\tau:=\hbar t/(2m)=\frac{tc}{\hbar}$,
$$e^{-itH/\hbar}=e^{-i\tau A},\qquad e^{-itH_{0}/\hbar}=e^{-i\tau A_{0}},$$
where the exponentials are those of
[[lem-self-adjoint-operator-generates-a-strongly-continuous-unitary-group]];

(d) let $F:\mathbb R\to\mathcal B(L^{2})$ be any family of bounded operators and
$\tau(t):=\hbar t/(2m)$. For every $\psi\in L^{2}$ the strong limit
$\lim_{t\to\pm\infty}F(\tau(t))\psi$ exists if and only if
$\lim_{\tau\to\pm\infty}F(\tau)\psi$ exists, and then the two limits are equal;
in particular
$$\operatorname*{s-lim}_{t\to\pm\infty}e^{itH/\hbar}e^{-itH_{0}/\hbar} =\operatorname*{s-lim}_{\tau\to\pm\infty}e^{i\tau A}e^{-i\tau A_{0}}$$
in the sense that either strong limit exists exactly when the other does, and
then they are equal;

(e) $\mu^{H}_{\psi}$ is absolutely continuous with respect to Lebesgue measure
if and only if $\mu^{A}_{\psi}$ is, and likewise for singularity with respect
to Lebesgue measure and for absence of atoms; and $\psi\ne0$ is an eigenvector
of $H$ with eigenvalue $\lambda$ if and only if it is an eigenvector of $A$
with eigenvalue $\lambda/c$.

The statement is an operator identity and a statement about spectral measures;
no physical interpretation, no scattering limit and no cross section is
asserted.

step_quotes.quote: 1.3 Put $m_c(\lambda)=c\lambda$ and, for Borel $B$, $F(B):=E_A(m_c^{-1}(B))=E_A(B/c)$. Preimages preserve intersections and countable disjoint unions, so [F4] gives the projection, identity and strong countable-additivity axioms for $F$. For every $x$, $F_x(B)=E_{A,x}(B/c)$. This scalar measure is regular: a compact $K\subseteq B/c$ approximating $E_{A,x}(B/c)$ transports to the compact $cK\subseteq B$ with the same measure, and an open $U\supseteq B/c$ with arbitrarily small excess transports to the open $cU\supseteq B$ with the same excess. These follow from regularity of $E_{A,x}$ and the homeomorphism $m_c$. Thus $F$ is a regular PVM, with the preimage direction appropriate to scaling $A$ by $c$. [F4, algebra]

step_quotes.quote: 3.1 Let $g_n(\lambda):=\lambda\mathbf1_{\{|\lambda|\le n\}}$. Step 2.1 gives $\Phi_F(g_n)=\Phi_{E_A}\bigl(c\lambda\mathbf1_{\{|c\lambda|\le n\}}\bigr)$; the cutoff is $|c\lambda|\le n$, not $|\lambda|\le n$. Its squared-norm identity and [F7] applied to the increasing squared cutoffs give $\int\lambda^2dF_x=c^2\int\lambda^2dE_{A,x}$, including possibly infinite values, for every $x$. Thus the identity-integral domain for $F$ is exactly $D(A)$ by [F4], [F5]. On that domain, the bounded functions $k_n(\lambda):=\lambda\mathbf1_{\{|c\lambda|\le n\}}$ approach $\lambda$ pointwise and satisfy $|k_n|\le|\lambda|$, so the actual cutoff-convergence clause of [F5] gives $\Phi_{E_A}(k_n)x\to Ax$. Therefore $\int\lambda\,dF\,x=\lim_n\Phi_F(g_n)x=c\lim_n\Phi_{E_A}(k_n)x=cAx$. The domain and action both match $cA$. [F4, F5, F7, step 2.1, algebra]

5.1 By [F7], $m_c$ and its inverse preserve Lebesgue null sets. Step 4.1 transports each scalar measure by this bijection, so a measure vanishes on every null set exactly when its counterpart does; a measure supported on a null set transports to one supported on the scaled null set, and conversely. Point masses satisfy $\mu^H_\psi(\{\lambda\})=\mu^A_\psi(\{\lambda/c\})$, so absence of atoms is preserved as well. On the common domain, $H\psi=cA\psi$ makes $H\psi=\lambda\psi$ equivalent to $A\psi=(\lambda/c)\psi$ for $\psi\ne0$, proving (e). [F7, step 1.2, step 4.1, algebra]

## Statement

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]). Let
$m,\hbar>0$, let $\Omega\subseteq\mathbb R^{3}$ and $I\subseteq\mathbb R$ be
nonempty open sets ([[def-interval]]), and let
$u,v:\Omega\times I\to\mathbb R$ be functions of class $C^{2}$
([[def-ck-euclidean-maps-and-diffeomorphisms]]) that satisfy the two real
equations
$$\hbar\,\partial_{t}u=-\frac{\hbar^{2}}{2m}\Delta v+Vv,\qquad -\hbar\,\partial_{t}v=-\frac{\hbar^{2}}{2m}\Delta u+Vu$$
pointwise on $\Omega\times I$ for a real-valued function $V$ on $\Omega\times
I$, where $\Delta=\partial_{1}^{2}+\partial_{2}^{2}+\partial_{3}^{2}$
([[def-directional-and-partial-derivatives]]) and where the equations are the
componentwise reading of
$i\hbar\,\partial_{t}\psi=-\frac{\hbar^{2}}{2m}\Delta\psi+V\psi$ for
$\psi:=u+iv$. Put
$$n:=u^{2}+v^{2}:\Omega\times I\to\mathbb R,\qquad \mathbf j:=\frac{\hbar}{m}\bigl(u\,\nabla v-v\,\nabla u\bigr):\Omega\times I\to\mathbb R^{3},$$
with $\nabla$ the gradient of [[def-jacobian-matrix-and-gradient]] and
$\operatorname{div}$ the divergence of
[[def-divergence-and-curl-of-a-c1-vector-field]]. Then:

(a) *Continuity identity.* $\partial_{t}n+\operatorname{div}\mathbf j=0$
pointwise on $\Omega\times I$.

(b) *Stationary solutions.* If $u,v:\Omega\to\mathbb R$ are $C^{2}$ and
independent of $t$, if $V:\Omega\to\mathbb R$ is real, and if there is a real
$E$ with
$$-\frac{\hbar^{2}}{2m}\Delta u+Vu=Eu,\qquad -\frac{\hbar^{2}}{2m}\Delta v+Vv=Ev$$
pointwise on $\Omega$, then $\operatorname{div}\mathbf j=0$ on $\Omega$ for the
time-independent field $\mathbf j=\frac{\hbar}{m}(u\nabla v-v\nabla u)$, and for
every closed ball $\overline{B(a,r)}\subseteq\Omega$ with outward unit normal
$\nu$ on the sphere $\partial B(a,r)$,
$$\int_{\partial B(a,r)}\mathbf j\cdot\nu\,dS=0 .$$

(c) *The two explicit readings.* Let $k>0$, $d\in S^{2}$ and define
$u(x):=\cos(kd\cdot x)$, $v(x):=\sin(kd\cdot x)$ on $\Omega=\mathbb R^{3}$
(then $u,v$ are $C^{\infty}$ and satisfy the stationary equations with $V=0$,
$E=\hbar^{2}k^{2}/(2m)$). Then
$$\mathbf j=\frac{\hbar k}{m}\,d\qquad\text{on }\mathbb R^{3}.$$
Let $r_{0}>0$, write $\Omega:=\{x\in\mathbb R^{3}:|x|>r_{0}\}$, let
$\Omega\ni x=r\,\omega$ with $r=|x|$, $\omega\in S^{2}$, and let
$a,b:S^{2}\to\mathbb R$ be functions with $a,b\in C^{1}$; define
$$u(x):=\frac{a(\omega)\cos(kr)-b(\omega)\sin(kr)}{r},\qquad v(x):=\frac{a(\omega)\sin(kr)+b(\omega)\cos(kr)}{r}$$
on $\Omega$, so that $u+iv=\frac{f(\omega)}{r}e^{ikr}$ with $f:=a+ib$. Then
$u,v\in C^{1}(\Omega)$ and, with $\hat r:=\omega$,
$$\mathbf j\cdot\hat r=\frac{\hbar k}{m}\frac{|f(\omega)|^{2}}{r^{2}},\qquad \text{equivalently}\qquad r^{2}\,\mathbf j\cdot\hat r=\frac{\hbar k}{m}|f(\omega)|^{2},$$
and the current identity holds for every declared $f\in C^{1}(S^{2})$, with no
equation required of the field.

The assertion is an identity for the declared differentiable functions; it
constructs no probability law, no state, no beam and no cross section. The
fields of clause (c) are only $C^{1}$: an $f\in C^{1}(S^{2})$ need not admit
two angular derivatives, and no outgoing field is claimed here to solve the
free equation or to be stationary.

## Statement

Adopt the declared short-range scattering model
[[def-nrqm-scattering-framework-short-range-model]] with mass parameter $m>0$,
spin zero, action constant $\hbar>0$, and a declared potential $V$ of the
**compact-support class**, so that $V$ is real, bounded and vanishes almost
everywhere outside a ball $B_{R}$; let $H^{\mathrm{free}}$ and
$H=H^{\mathrm{free}}+M_{V}$ be the assigned energy observables of the model on
$D(H)=W^{2,2}(\mathbb R^{3};\mathbb C)$, and let $\Omega_{\pm}$, $S$,
$\mu^{H}_{\psi}$ and $H_{\mathrm{ac}}(H)$ be as in clause (d) of that
definition. Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice
([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Then:

(a) $H$ is self-adjoint on $D(H)=W^{2,2}(\mathbb R^{3};\mathbb C)$ and bounded
below, and for every Schwartz function $\psi\in\mathcal S(\mathbb R^{3};\mathbb C)$
([[def-schwartz-space-and-its-seminorms]])
$$\int_{0}^{\infty}\bigl\|Ve^{-itH^{\mathrm{free}}/\hbar}\psi\bigr\|_{2}\,dt<\infty, \qquad \int_{-\infty}^{0}\bigl\|Ve^{-itH^{\mathrm{free}}/\hbar}\psi\bigr\|_{2}\,dt<\infty;$$

(b) the strong limits
$$\Omega_{\pm}=\operatorname*{s-lim}_{t\to\pm\infty}e^{itH/\hbar}e^{-itH^{\mathrm{free}}/\hbar}$$
exist as bounded linear isometries of $H_{0}$, so $\Omega_{\pm}^{*}\Omega_{\pm}=I$;
they intertwine the two flows,
$$e^{-isH/\hbar}\Omega_{\pm}=\Omega_{\pm}e^{-isH^{\mathrm{free}}/\hbar}\qquad(s\in\mathbb R),$$
and satisfy $H\Omega_{\pm}\psi=\Omega_{\pm}H^{\mathrm{free}}\psi$ for every
$\psi\in D(H^{\mathrm{free}})$;

(c) the free operator has purely absolutely continuous spectrum: for every
$\psi\in H_{0}$ the scalar measure $\mu^{H^{\mathrm{free}}}_{\psi}$ is
absolutely continuous with respect to Lebesgue measure and gives zero mass to
$\{0\}$ and to $(-\infty,0)$; hence
$H_{\mathrm{ac}}(H^{\mathrm{free}})=H_{\mathrm c}(H^{\mathrm{free}})=H_{0}$
and $H^{\mathrm{free}}$ has no eigenvalues;

(d) $H$ has no eigenvalue in $(0,\infty)$: if $\psi\in D(H)$, $\psi\ne0$ and
$H\psi=\lambda\psi$ with $\lambda>0$, then no such $\psi$ exists.

The statement is conditional on the declared model and the cited mathematics.
It asserts no completeness of the ranges, no unitarity of $S$, no cross
section and no measured quantity; completeness is the content of the two
following theorems of this page.

## Statement

**compact-support class**, so that $V$ is real, bounded and vanishes almost
everywhere outside a ball $B_{R}$; let $H^{\mathrm{free}}$ and
$H=H^{\mathrm{free}}+M_{V}$ be the assigned energy observables of the model on
$D(H)=W^{2,2}(\mathbb R^{3};\mathbb C)$, and let $\Omega_{\pm}$, $S$,
$\mu^{H}_{\psi}$ and $H_{\mathrm{ac}}(H)$ be as in clause (d) of that
definition. Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice
([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Then:

(a) $H$ is self-adjoint on $D(H)=W^{2,2}(\mathbb R^{3};\mathbb C)$ and bounded
below, and for every Schwartz function $\psi\in\mathcal S(\mathbb R^{3};\mathbb C)$
([[def-schwartz-space-and-its-seminorms]])
$$\int_{0}^{\infty}\bigl\|Ve^{-itH^{\mathrm{free}}/\hbar}\psi\bigr\|_{2}\,dt<\infty, \qquad \int_{-\infty}^{0}\bigl\|Ve^{-itH^{\mathrm{free}}/\hbar}\psi\bigr\|_{2}\,dt<\infty;$$

$$\Omega_{\pm}=\operatorname*{s-lim}_{t\to\pm\infty}e^{itH/\hbar}e^{-itH^{\mathrm{free}}/\hbar}$$
exist as bounded linear isometries of $H_{0}$, so $\Omega_{\pm}^{*}\Omega_{\pm}=I$;

$$e^{-isH/\hbar}\Omega_{\pm}=\Omega_{\pm}e^{-isH^{\mathrm{free}}/\hbar}\qquad(s\in\mathbb R),$$
and satisfy $H\Omega_{\pm}\psi=\Omega_{\pm}H^{\mathrm{free}}\psi$ for every
$\psi\in D(H^{\mathrm{free}})$;

$\psi\in H_{0}$ the scalar measure $\mu^{H^{\mathrm{free}}}_{\psi}$ is
absolutely continuous with respect to Lebesgue measure and gives zero mass to
$\{0\}$ and to $(-\infty,0)$; hence
$H_{\mathrm{ac}}(H^{\mathrm{free}})=H_{\mathrm c}(H^{\mathrm{free}})=H_{0}$
and $H^{\mathrm{free}}$ has no eigenvalues;

$H\psi=\lambda\psi$ with $\lambda>0$, then no such $\psi$ exists.

## Statement

Adopt the declared short-range scattering model
[[def-nrqm-scattering-framework-short-range-model]] with mass $m>0$, spin
zero, action constant $\hbar>0$ and a declared **compact-support-class**
potential $V$ supported in a ball $B_{R}$. Let $\Omega_{\pm}$ and $S$ be the
wave operators and scattering operator of clause (d) of that definition,
$E_{H}$ the projection valued measure of the self-adjoint interacting operator
$H$, and $\mu^{H}_{\psi}$ its scalar measures. Assume the Axiom of Countable
Choice and the Axiom of Choice ([[def-countable-choice]],
[[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Then:

(a) the wave operators exist by
[[pthm-nrqm-scattering-wave-operator-existence-and-free-continuity]], and
$\operatorname{ran}\Omega_{\pm}\subseteq H_{\mathrm{ac}}(H)$ and
$H_{\mathrm{sc}}(H)=\{0\}$, where
$$H_{\mathrm{sc}}(H):=\{\psi\in H_{0}:\mu^{H}_{\psi}\ \text{is atomless and singular with respect to Lebesgue measure}\};$$

(b) each wave operator is asymptotically complete,
$$\operatorname{ran}\Omega_{+}=\operatorname{ran}\Omega_{-}=H_{\mathrm{ac}}(H)=H_{\mathrm c}(H);$$

(c) $S=\Omega_{+}^{*}\Omega_{-}$ is unitary on $H_{0}$ and commutes with the
free flow, $Se^{-itH^{\mathrm{free}}/\hbar}=e^{-itH^{\mathrm{free}}/\hbar}S$ for
every $t\in\mathbb R$.

The statement is a conditional consequence of the declared model with a
compactly supported real bounded potential; it asserts no stationary amplitude,
no partial-wave decomposition, no cross section and no measured quantity.

## Statement

Adopt the declared short-range scattering model
[[def-nrqm-scattering-framework-short-range-model]] with mass $m>0$, spin
zero, action constant $\hbar>0$, and a declared potential $V$ of the
**resolvent-tail class**: real $V=V_{2}+V_{\mathrm b}$ with
$V_{2}\in L^{2}(\mathbb R^{3})$ and $V_{\mathrm b}\in L^{\infty}(\mathbb R^{3})$
real, and, with the reduced potential $W:=2mV/\hbar^{2}$ and the
nondimensional free operator $A_{0}:=-\Delta_{w}$ of the model,
$$h(r):=\bigl\|M_{W}(A_{0}-i)^{-1}\mathbf 1_{\{|x|\ge r\}}\bigr\|,$$
finite for every $r\ge0$ and in $L^{1}([0,\infty))$.
Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice
([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Then:

(a) $H=H^{\mathrm{free}}+M_{V}$ is self-adjoint on
$D(H)=W^{2,2}(\mathbb R^{3};\mathbb C)$
([[def-sobolev-space-wkp-and-its-norm]]); both wave operators
$$\Omega_{\pm}=\operatorname*{s-lim}_{t\to\pm\infty}e^{itH/\hbar}e^{-itH^{\mathrm{free}}/\hbar}$$
exist as bounded linear isometries, $\operatorname{ran}\Omega_{+}=\operatorname{ran}\Omega_{-}
=H_{\mathrm{ac}}(H)=H_{\mathrm c}(H)$, and $H_{\mathrm{sc}}(H)=\{0\}$;

(b) $S=\Omega_{+}^{*}\Omega_{-}$ is unitary on $H_{0}$;

(c) the conclusions of (a) and (b) hold in particular for a declared potential
of the explicit **decaying-tail form** $V=V_{\mathrm{loc}}+V_{\mathrm{tail}}$
with real $V_{\mathrm{loc}}\in L^{2}(\mathbb R^{3})$ compactly supported and
$|V_{\mathrm{tail}}(x)|\le C(1+|x|)^{-1-\delta}$ almost everywhere for some
constants $C>0$, $\delta>0$; here the integrability hypothesis of the preamble
is not presupposed, because the cited theorem supplies it for this form;

(d) the explicit decaying-tail form of (c) does not cover the pure Coulomb
potential $V(x)=-\kappa/|x|$, $\kappa>0$: after any split into a compactly
supported $L^{2}$ part and a tail part, the bound
$|V_{\mathrm{tail}}(x)|\le C(1+|x|)^{-1-\delta}$ fails for every $\delta>0$,
because $\kappa(1+|x|)^{1+\delta}/|x|\to+\infty$ as $|x|\to\infty$. The pure Coulomb potential also fails the general resolvent-tail integrability hypothesis itself, as proved below; the Coulomb case is the separate
declared long-range model of this page.

The statement is conditional on the declared model with the displayed
integrability hypothesis and the cited mathematics; no cross section,
stationary amplitude or measured quantity is asserted.

step_quotes.quote: 1.1 Put $W:=2mV/\hbar^{2}=W_{2}+W_{\mathrm b}$ with $W_{2}:=(2m/\hbar^{2})V_{2}\in L^{2}$ and $W_{\mathrm b}:=(2m/\hbar^{2})V_{\mathrm b}\in L^{\infty}$, both real. The nondimensional free operator $A_{0}=-\Delta_{w}$ is the operator written $-\Delta$ on $H^{2}(\mathbb R^{3};\mathbb C)$ in [F2], and the class definition gives that $\|M_{W}(A_{0}-i)^{-1}\mathbf 1_{\{|\cdot|\ge r\}}\|$ is finite for every $r$ and integrable in $r$; hence [F2] applies with $V_{0}=W$ and gives: $A:=-\Delta+M_{W}$ is self-adjoint on $H^{2}$, both nondimensional wave operators exist, $H_{\mathrm{sc}}(A)=\{0\}$, $\operatorname{ran}\Omega_{+}=\operatorname{ran}\Omega_{-}=H_{\mathrm{ac}}(A)=H_{\mathrm c}(A)$, and $S_{\mathrm{nd}}=\Omega_{+}^{*}\Omega_{-}$ is unitary. 2.1 By [F1] the model's operators are $H=cA$, $H^{\mathrm{free}}=cA_{0}$ on $W^{2,2}$ with $c=\hbar^{2}/(2m)$, so $H$ is self-adjoint on $D(H)=W^{2,2}(\mathbb R^{3};\mathbb C)$, the physical strong limits exist exactly when the nondimensional ones do and then coincide, and the subspaces $H_{\mathrm{ac}},H_{\mathrm{sc}},H_{\mathrm c}$ of $H$ and $A$ agree; moreover every operator $e^{itH/\hbar}e^{-itH^{\mathrm{free}}/\hbar}$ is unitary, so for every $\psi$ the strong limit satisfies $\|\Omega_{\pm}\psi\|=\lim_{t\to\pm\infty}\|e^{itH/\hbar}e^{-itH^{\mathrm{free}}/\hbar}\psi\|=\|\psi\|$, i.e. $\Omega_{\pm}$ are isometries. Combining with step 1.1 gives (a). [F1, step 1.1, algebra]

$\mathrm{m^{-3}}$, with incident energy $E=\hbar^2k^2/(2m)$.
The construction below retains the dimensionless unit-incident shape
$\Psi$; its physical beam field is $\Phi=\sqrt{n_{\mathrm{inc}}}\Psi$.
Put
$$W:=\frac{2m}{\hbar^{2}}V,\qquad G_{k}(z):=\frac{e^{ik|z|}}{4\pi|z|},\qquad (K_{k}f)(x):=\int_{B_{R}}G_{k}(x-y)W(y)f(y)\,dy$$
for $f\in L^{2}(B_{R};\mathbb C)$ and $x\in B_{R}$. Assume the Axiom of
Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice ([[def-countable-choice]],
[[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Then:

(a) $I+K_{k}$ is boundedly invertible on $L^{2}(B_{R};\mathbb C)$; with
$u:=(I+K_{k})^{-1}\bigl(e^{ikd\cdot x}|_{B_{R}}\bigr)$ and
$$\Psi(x):=e^{ikd\cdot x}-\int_{B_{R}}G_{k}(x-y)W(y)u(y)\,dy,$$
one has $\Psi\in H^{2}_{\mathrm{loc}}(\mathbb R^{3})$,
$(-\Delta+W-k^{2})\Psi=0$ distributionally on $\mathbb R^{3}$, and
$\Psi|_{B_{R}}=u$;

(b) with $r=|x|>2R$ and $\Omega=x/r$, the **scattering amplitude**
$$f_{k}(\Omega):=-\frac{1}{4\pi}\int_{B_{R}}e^{-ik\Omega\cdot y}W(y)u(y)\,dy$$
is smooth on $S^{2}$ and
$$\Psi(x)=e^{ikd\cdot x}+\frac{e^{ikr}f_{k}(\Omega)}{r}+\mathcal E(x),$$
where $|\mathcal E(x)|+|\partial_{r}\mathcal E(x)|\le C(k,R,\|Wu\|_{1})r^{-2}$

all_current_steps.quote: 1.1 Since $V$ is real, bounded and supported in $B_{R}$, so is $W=2mV/\hbar^{2}$, which is read in $\mathrm{m^{-2}}$; dividing the physical stationary equation $-\frac{\hbar^{2}}{2m}\Delta\Psi+V\Psi=E\Psi$ by $c=\hbar^{2}/(2m)$ gives $-\Delta\Psi+W\Psi=(E/c)\Psi$, and $E/c=\hbar^{2}k^{2}/(2m)\cdot2m/\hbar^{2}=k^{2}$ by [F3] with $E=\hbar^{2}k^{2}/(2m)$. [F3, given, algebra]

2.1 The kernel $G_{k}(x-y)W(y)$ on $B_{R}\times B_{R}$ is square-integrable because $|x-y|^{-2}$ is locally integrable in three dimensions and $B_{R}$ is bounded, so $K_{k}$ is Hilbert-Schmidt and [F2] gives bounded invertibility of $I+K_{k}$; [F1] then gives $\Psi\in H^{2}_{\mathrm{loc}}$, the distributional equation $(-\Delta+W-k^{2})\Psi=0$ and $\Psi|_{B_{R}}=u$, which is (a). [F2, F1, step 1.1, algebra]

3.1 By [F1] the smooth amplitude $f_{k}(\Omega)=-(4\pi)^{-1}\int e^{-ik\Omega\cdot y}W(y)u(y)dy$ and the uniform expansion with the $r^{-2}$ remainder and its tangential and radial derivative bounds hold; these are exactly the displays of (b), with the constant depending on $k,R$ and $\|Wu\|_{1}$. [F1, step 2.1]

4.1 By [F1] the unit-shape scattered field $\Psi_{\mathrm{sc}}=\Psi-e^{ikd\cdot x}$ has radial mathematical current $(\hbar k/m)|f_k|^2/r^2+O(r^{-3})$ uniformly. Since the scale is constant, its current is $(\hbar/m)[(\sqrt{n_{\mathrm{inc}}}u)
abla(\sqrt{n_{\mathrm{inc}}}v)-(\sqrt{n_{\mathrm{inc}}}v)
abla(\sqrt{n_{\mathrm{inc}}}u)]=n_{\mathrm{inc}}(\hbar/m)(u
abla v-v
abla u)$ by [F4]. Thus the physical scattered current is the display in (c), and the same calculation on the unit incident plane wave gives $J_{\mathrm{inc}}=n_{\mathrm{inc}}\hbar k/m>0$. Dividing yields $\lim_{r	o\infty}r^2j_r^{\mathrm{sc}}/J_{\mathrm{inc}}=|f_k|^2$. Smoothness and boundedness of $f_k$ on the sphere, with [F1]'s uniform error, give the finite total cross section $\sigma=\int_{S^2}|f_k|^2d\Omega$. 5.1 By step 2.1 and step 3.1 the constructed $\Psi$ is $C^{2}$ on the complement of the essential closed support of $V$: near each such point the convolution integrates the compactly supported $L^1$ density $Wu$ against $G_k(x-y)$ at a positive distance from its singularity, so its derivatives of every fixed order are bounded on a smaller neighborhood and differentiation under that integral is valid; the incident exponential is smooth too, satisfies the stationary equation there and has the outgoing reading with amplitude $f_{k}$ in metres; by [F5] it is a generalized stationary solution of the beam model at energy $E$ and direction $d$, and the construction determines it through the explicit invertible problem, so no other function with the same equation and outgoing reading arises from this construction. ## Statement

Adopt the declared short-range scattering model
[[def-nrqm-scattering-framework-short-range-model]] with mass $m>0$, spin
zero and a **declared central short-range potential** $V(x)=v(|x|)$ in the
sense of [[def-nrqm-scattering-partial-wave-and-phase-shift-readings]]
clause (a): $v$ is real, bounded and $V$ is supported in a ball $B_{R}$. Adopt
the stationary elastic beam model at wave number $k>0$ and direction
$d\in S^{2}$, with amplitude $f_{k}$ as in
[[pthm-nrqm-scattering-stationary-wave-amplitude-and-flux]], and the
channel vocabulary of
[[def-nrqm-scattering-partial-wave-and-phase-shift-readings]] clauses (b),
(c). Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice
([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Then:

(a) $f_{k}$ depends only on $\cos\theta=\Omega\cdot d$, and its **Legendre
expansion**
$$f_{k}(\theta)=\frac{1}{2ik}\sum_{l\ge0}(2l+1)\bigl(S_{l}(k)-1\bigr)P_{l}(\cos\theta)$$
converges in $L^{2}(S^{2})$ and absolutely, so the model's cross-section
reading is
$$\frac{d\sigma}{d\Omega}(\theta)=|f_{k}(\theta)|^{2};$$

(b) the channel factors are unit modulus, $|S_{l}(k)|=1$, the phase shifts
$\delta_{l}(k)$ are real modulo $\pi$, and the **total cross section** of the
beam model is
$$\sigma=\frac{\pi}{k^{2}}\sum_{l\ge0}(2l+1)|S_{l}(k)-1|^{2} =\frac{4\pi}{k^{2}}\sum_{l\ge0}(2l+1)\sin^{2}\delta_{l}(k)\qquad\text{in }\mathrm{m^{2}},$$
the series converging, with the channel readings of
[[def-nrqm-scattering-partial-wave-and-phase-shift-readings]] clause (c) as
its summands;

(c) the objects $\varphi_{l}$, $f_{l}$, $S_{l}$ and $\delta_{l}$ of the
channel vocabulary are exactly the regular and outgoing radial solutions, the
Wronskian ratio and the phase shift constructed by the cited mathematics for
the reduced radial potential $w=(2m/\hbar^2)v$ at the model's wave number $k$; the phase shifts
are not asserted to have a definite sign and no low-energy limit is asserted
beyond the convergence of the series.

The statement is conditional on the declared central model, the beam model
and the cited mathematics; it asserts no measured angular distribution and no
identification of $l$ with a measured angular momentum.

## Statement

Adopt the declared short-range scattering model
[[def-nrqm-scattering-framework-short-range-model]] with mass $m>0$, spin
zero and a **compact-support-class** potential $V$ supported in $B_{R}$, adopt
the stationary elastic beam model at wave number $k>0$ and direction
$d\in S^{2}$, and let
$$W:=\frac{2m}{\hbar^{2}}V,\qquad G_{k}(z)=\frac{e^{ik|z|}}{4\pi|z|},\qquad (K_{k}f)(x)=\int_{B_{R}}G_{k}(x-y)W(y)f(y)\,dy$$
and $u=(I+K_{k})^{-1}e_{\mathrm{inc}}$, $f_{k}$ be as in
[[pthm-nrqm-scattering-stationary-wave-amplitude-and-flux]], with
$e_{\mathrm{inc}}=e^{ikd\cdot x}|_{B_{R}}$. Put $q:=\|K_{k}\|$, the operator
norm of [[def-operator-norm]] and [[def-bounded-linear-operator]], and
$$f_{B}(\Omega):=-\frac{1}{4\pi}\int_{B_{R}}e^{ik(d-\Omega)\cdot y}W(y)\,dy$$
for $\Omega\in S^{2}$, read in metres. Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice
and the Axiom of Choice ([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-axiom-of-choice]]).
Then:

(a) the operator $K_{k}$ is bounded, $q<\infty$, and if $q<1$ the exact
stationary solution satisfies
$$\bigl\|u-e_{\mathrm{inc}}\bigr\|_{L^{2}(B_{R})}\le\frac{q}{1-q}\, \bigl\|e_{\mathrm{inc}}\bigr\|_{L^{2}(B_{R})};$$

(b) under the same condition $q<1$ the **Born amplitude** $f_{B}$ approximates
the exact amplitude uniformly,
$$\bigl|f_{k}(\Omega)-f_{B}(\Omega)\bigr|\le \frac{\|W\|_{\infty}\,|B_{R}|^{1/2}}{4\pi}\,\frac{q}{1-q}\, \bigl\|e_{\mathrm{inc}}\bigr\|_{L^{2}(B_{R})} \qquad(\Omega\in S^{2}),$$
with $|B_{R}|=4\pi R^{3}/3$;

(c) *coupling scaling.* For a real or complex multiplier $\eta$ with
$|\eta|q<1$, let $u_{\eta}:=(I+\eta K_{k})^{-1}e_{\mathrm{inc}}$, let
$f_{k,\eta}(\Omega;d):=-\eta(4\pi)^{-1}\int_{B_R}e^{-ik\Omega\cdot y}W(y)u_\eta(y;d)\,dy$ be the amplitude for the scaled potential $\eta W$, and let $f_{B}$ be as above. Then
$$\bigl\|u_{\eta}-e_{\mathrm{inc}}\bigr\|_{2}\le\frac{|\eta|q}{1-|\eta|q} \bigl\|e_{\mathrm{inc}}\bigr\|_{2},\qquad \sup_{\Omega,d\in S^{2}}\bigl|f_{k,\eta}(\Omega;d)-\eta f_{B}(\Omega;d)\bigr| \le\frac{|\eta|^{2}\|W\|_{\infty}|B_{R}|q}{4\pi(1-|\eta|q)};$$
in particular no condition on the base operator norm of $K_{k}$ itself is
needed for (c).

The statement is conditional on the declared model and the cited mathematics;
the condition $q<1$ is an operator-norm condition on the declared potential,
kernel and wave number, not a vague smallness of $V$, and no measured cross
section is asserted.

## Statement

Adopt the declared short-range scattering model
[[def-nrqm-scattering-framework-short-range-model]] with mass $m>0$, spin
zero and a **compact-support-class** potential $V$ supported in $B_{R}$; by
[[pthm-nrqm-scattering-compact-support-asymptotic-completeness]] the model's
wave operators exist and
$$S=\Omega_{+}^{*}\Omega_{-}$$
is unitary on $H_{0}$ and commutes with the free flow. Write $\sigma$ for
surface measure on $S^{2}$ and $\mathfrak h=L^{2}(S^{2},d\sigma)$, and for
every $d\in S^{2}$ let $f_{k}(\cdot,d)$ be the model's stationary amplitude
of [[pthm-nrqm-scattering-stationary-wave-amplitude-and-flux]] at incident
direction $d$, with the operator $\mathcal A_{k}$ on $\mathfrak h$ defined by
$$(\mathcal A_{k}a)(\Omega):=\int_{S^{2}}f_{k}(\Omega,d)\,a(d)\,d\sigma(d).$$
Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice
([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Then:

(a) the free flow is diagonalized by the free trace transform of the cited
mathematics, a unitary $F_{0}:H_{0}\to L^{2}((0,\infty),dE;\mathfrak h)$ with
$(F_{0}g)(E,\omega)=E^{1/4}2^{-1/2}\widehat g(\sqrt E\,\omega)$ in the
nondimensional variables of the scaling correspondence, and the model's
scattering operator is carried into multiplication,
$$F_{0}\,S\,F_{0}^{*}=M_{S(E)};$$

(b) for almost every $E=k^{2}>0$ the on-shell operator is
$$S(E)=I+\frac{ik}{2\pi}\mathcal A_{k},$$
a unitary operator on $\mathfrak h$, and the model's stationary amplitude
$f_{k}(\Omega,d)$ is the kernel of $\mathcal A_{k}$;

(c) for $R\in SO(3)$ let $V_{R}(x):=V(R^{-1}x)$ and $(U_{R}a)(\omega):=a(R^{-1}\omega)$;
then
$$S[V_{R}](E)=U_{R}\,S[V](E)\,U_{R}^{-1};$$

(d) if $V$ is in addition central, the fiber decomposes in the spherical
harmonic basis as $S(E)Y_{lm}=S_{l}(k)Y_{lm}$, where $S_{l}$ and
$\delta_{l}$ are the model's channel factor and phase shift of
[[def-nrqm-scattering-partial-wave-and-phase-shift-readings]], equal to the
Wronskian ratio $\overline{W(\varphi_{l},f_{l})}/W(\varphi_{l},f_{l})$, and
the cross-section reading of
[[pthm-nrqm-scattering-partial-wave-cross-section]] is the phase-shift series
of that channel decomposition.

The statement identifies operators and operators-valued functions of the
declared model; it asserts no measurement of $S$ or $S(E)$, no detector model
and no empirical claim.

[F1, F2, given]

2.1 By [F2] the model's stationary amplitude for direction $d$ is the amplitude of [F1]'s stationary problem for $W$ at the same wave number $k$; hence $\mathcal A_{k}$ is exactly the on-shell amplitude operator of [F1]. [F1, F2, step 1.1]

3.1 By [F1] the free trace transform $F_{0}$ diagonalizes the free flow and $F_{0}SF_{0}^{*}=M_{S(E)}$ with $S(E)=I+\frac{ik}{2\pi}\mathcal A_{k}$; since the model's $S$ and $\mathcal A_{k}$ are the same operators as in [F1] by steps 1.1 and 2.1, the displays of (a) and (b) follow, including unitarity of the on-shell operator. 5.1 If $V$ is central, so is $W$; [F1] gives $S(E)Y_{lm}=S_{l}(k)Y_{lm}$ with $S_{l}=\overline{W_{l}}/W_{l}$; by [F3] the model's channel vocabulary names exactly these objects $S_{l}=\overline{W(\varphi_{l},f_{l})}/W(\varphi_{l},f_{l})$ and $\delta_{l}$, and the phase-shift series of the partial-wave theorem is the total cross-section reading of this decomposition. ## Statement

Adopt the declared long-range Coulomb model
[[def-nrqm-scattering-coulomb-dollard-model]] with mass $m>0$, spin zero,
action constant $\hbar>0$, coupling $\kappa>0$, the assigned energy operator
$H_{\kappa}$ on $H^{2}(\mathbb R^{3};\mathbb C)$, the free operator
$H^{\mathrm{free}}$, the inverse-length coupling
$\gamma=2m\kappa/\hbar^{2}$, a declared reference length $\ell_\star>0$ in metres and reference time $t_{\star}=2m\ell_\star^2/\hbar$, the
Dollard-modified comparison $U_{D}(t)$ and the modified wave operators
$\Omega_{D\pm}$ and $S_{D}$ of that definition. Assume the Axiom of Countable
Choice and the Axiom of Choice ([[def-countable-choice]],
[[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Then:

(a) the modified wave operators exist as strong limits and are bounded linear
isometries, $\Omega_{D\pm}^{*}\Omega_{D\pm}=I$, and they intertwine,
$$\Omega_{D\pm}e^{-isH^{\mathrm{free}}/\hbar}=e^{-isH_{\kappa}/\hbar}\Omega_{D\pm} \qquad(s\in\mathbb R);$$

(b) the modified wave operators are complete,
$$\operatorname{ran}\Omega_{D+}=\operatorname{ran}\Omega_{D-} =H_{\mathrm{ac}}(H_{\kappa})=H_{\mathrm c}(H_{\kappa});$$

(c) the modified scattering operator $S_{D}=\Omega_{D+}^{*}\Omega_{D-}$ is
unitary on $H_{0}$ and commutes with the free flow;

(d) the ordinary short-range comparison of the model is not substituted:
neither existence nor completeness of
$\operatorname*{s-lim}_{t\to\pm\infty}e^{itH_{\kappa}/\hbar}e^{-itH^{\mathrm{free}}/\hbar}$
is asserted, and the modification is essential to the statement.

The statement is conditional on the declared model and the cited
mathematics. It asserts no explicit Coulomb scattering amplitude, no
Rutherford or other cross section, and no measured quantity; the logarithmic
phase is a comparison construction for the long-range generator.

step_quotes.quote: 2.1 [Exact fixed energy phases] For a positive numerical energy $e=c_0\lambda$, the phase coefficient of the physical definition is $m_0k_0/(h_0\sqrt{2m_0e})=\gamma_0/(2\sqrt\lambda)$. By [F1], $a(P)=\gamma_0/(2|P|)$ for the numerical source $A_0=|P|^2$. For $\sigma\in\{+1,-1\}$ define the fixed bounded unitary $B_{\sigma,L}=b_{\sigma,L}(A_0),\qquad b_{\sigma,L}(\lambda)=\exp\Bigl(-2i\sigma\frac{\gamma_0}{2\sqrt\lambda}\log L\Bigr)\quad(\lambda>0),\qquad b_{\sigma,L}(0)=1.$ The functions are bounded unimodular Borel functions despite their oscillation near zero, so their calculus is defined on all $L^2$ and they commute with $e^{-irA_0}$ for every $r$. Spectral correspondence [F3] and step 1.1 give, for $|\tau|\ge1$ and $\sigma=\operatorname{sign}t$, $\mathcal J_0U_D(t)\mathcal J_0^{-1}=e^{-i\tau A_0}e^{i\sigma a(P)\log|\tau|}B_{\sigma,L}=U_D^{\mathrm{nd}}(\tau)B_{\sigma,L}.$ The bounded functional calculus also transports under $\mathcal J_0$: conjugating the PVM gives a regular PVM representing the numerical operator, so spectral uniqueness identifies it and simple-function approximation gives the claimed calculus transport. If desired, the annular smooth momentum class in [F1] is preserved by each $B_{\sigma,L}$ because its multiplier is smooth on every compact annulus; hence the source remainder estimate remains integrable on that class after this fixed phase. The comparison for finite $|\tau|<1$ need not equal the source's short-time extension and is irrelevant to the two asymptotic limits. [step 1.1, F1, F3, F4, algebra]

4.1 [Full completeness under the reference convention] Because $B_{\pm,L}$ are onto, step 3.1 gives $\operatorname{ran}\Omega_{D\pm}=\mathcal J_0^{-1}\operatorname{ran}W_\pm$. By [F2], this is $\mathcal J_0^{-1}H_{\mathrm{ac}}(C_{\gamma_0})=\mathcal J_0^{-1}H_{\mathrm c}(C_{\gamma_0})$. Positive energy scaling by $c_0$ preserves these spectral subspaces [F3], and the unitary numerical coordinate representation transports the spectral measures and their subspaces as in step 2.1. The resulting physical subspaces are exactly $H_{\mathrm{ac}}(H_\kappa)=H_{\mathrm c}(H_\kappa)$. This proves (b) for every declared reference length, preserving the source's whole continuous subspace and all angular channels. [step 2.1, step 3.1, F2, F3, algebra]

step_quotes.quote: 3.1 [Strong limits, isometry and intertwining] Apply [F2] at the positive numerical coupling $\gamma_0$. Let $W_\pm$ be its two full-space Dollard wave operators. all_current_steps.quote: 1.1 [Numerical SI comparison with dimensionless arguments] Write the fixed SI units as $L_0=1\,\mathrm m$, $T_0=1\,\mathrm s$, $M_0=1\,\mathrm{kg}$ and $E_0=1\,\mathrm J$. Let $m_0=m/M_0$, $h_0=\hbar/(E_0T_0)$, $k_0=\kappa/(E_0L_0)$, $L=\ell_\star/L_0>0$ and $t_0=t/T_0$ be their numerical values, and put $\gamma_0=\gamma L_0=2m_0k_0/h_0^2$, $c_0=h_0^2/(2m_0)$ and $\tau=h_0t_0/(2m_0)$. These are pure real numbers, with $\tau\to\pm\infty$ as $t\to\pm\infty$. Represent the wavefunctions in the numerical SI coordinate $q=x/L_0$, with the normalized $L^2$ coordinate map $\mathcal J_0f(q)=L_0^{3/2}f(L_0q)$, the Jacobian normalization understood in the chosen length unit. Substitution in the integral proves this map unitary; weak derivative substitution gives its exact $H^2$ domain transport. The numerical energy representatives are therefore $\mathsf H_\kappa=E_0^{-1}\mathcal J_0H_\kappa\mathcal J_0^{-1}=c_0C_{\gamma_0}$ and $\mathsf H_f=E_0^{-1}\mathcal J_0H^{\mathrm{free}}\mathcal J_0^{-1}=c_0A_0$, where $A_0=-\Delta_q$ and $C_{\gamma_0}=-\Delta_q-\gamma_0/|q|$. Thus $\mathcal J_0e^{-itH_\kappa/\hbar}\mathcal J_0^{-1}=e^{-i\tau C_{\gamma_0}}$ and similarly for the free operator. The numerical reference time is $t_{\star,0}=2m_0L^2/h_0$, so $\frac{|t|}{t_\star}=\frac{|t_0|}{t_{\star,0}}=\frac{|\tau|}{L^2},\qquad \log\frac{|t|}{t_\star}=\log|\tau|-2\log L.$ Every logarithm has a dimensionless argument; no time having units of length squared is placed inside the source logarithm. [F3, F4, given, algebra]

2.1 [Exact fixed energy phases] For a positive numerical energy $e=c_0\lambda$, the phase coefficient of the physical definition is $m_0k_0/(h_0\sqrt{2m_0e})=\gamma_0/(2\sqrt\lambda)$. By [F1], $a(P)=\gamma_0/(2|P|)$ for the numerical source $A_0=|P|^2$. For $\sigma\in\{+1,-1\}$ define the fixed bounded unitary $B_{\sigma,L}=b_{\sigma,L}(A_0),\qquad b_{\sigma,L}(\lambda)=\exp\Bigl(-2i\sigma\frac{\gamma_0}{2\sqrt\lambda}\log L\Bigr)\quad(\lambda>0),\qquad b_{\sigma,L}(0)=1.$ The functions are bounded unimodular Borel functions despite their oscillation near zero, so their calculus is defined on all $L^2$ and they commute with $e^{-irA_0}$ for every $r$. Spectral correspondence [F3] and step 1.1 give, for $|\tau|\ge1$ and $\sigma=\operatorname{sign}t$, $\mathcal J_0U_D(t)\mathcal J_0^{-1}=e^{-i\tau A_0}e^{i\sigma a(P)\log|\tau|}B_{\sigma,L}=U_D^{\mathrm{nd}}(\tau)B_{\sigma,L}.$ The bounded functional calculus also transports under $\mathcal J_0$: conjugating the PVM gives a regular PVM representing the numerical operator, so spectral uniqueness identifies it and simple-function approximation gives the claimed calculus transport. If desired, the annular smooth momentum class in [F1] is preserved by each $B_{\sigma,L}$ because its multiplier is smooth on every compact annulus; hence the source remainder estimate remains integrable on that class after this fixed phase. The comparison for finite $|\tau|<1$ need not equal the source's short-time extension and is irrelevant to the two asymptotic limits. [step 1.1, F1, F3, F4, algebra]

3.1 [Strong limits, isometry and intertwining] Apply [F2] at the positive numerical coupling $\gamma_0$. Let $W_\pm$ be its two full-space Dollard wave operators. Step 2.1 makes the physical comparison product, conjugated by $\mathcal J_0$, equal $e^{i\tau C_{\gamma_0}}U_D^{\mathrm{nd}}(\tau)B_{\pm,L}$ on the corresponding exterior half-line. The fixed bounded right factor and the positive scalar time change let the strong limits pass on every vector, giving $\Omega_{D\pm}=\mathcal J_0^{-1}W_\pm B_{\pm,L}\mathcal J_0.$ Both $W_\pm$ are isometries by [F2] and both $B_{\pm,L}$ are unitaries, so these operators are isometries. For physical $s\in\mathbb R$, put $r=h_0(s/T_0)/(2m_0)$. The numerical free/Coulomb flows are $e^{-irA_0}$ and $e^{-irC_{\gamma_0}}$ by step 1.1. Since $B_{\pm,L}$ commute with the free flow and $W_\pm e^{-irA_0}=e^{-irC_{\gamma_0}}W_\pm$, conjugating gives the exact intertwining of (a). No new source existence or momentum-domain assumption was introduced. [step 1.1, step 2.1, F2, F3, algebra]

4.1 [Full completeness under the reference convention] Because $B_{\pm,L}$ are onto, step 3.1 gives $\operatorname{ran}\Omega_{D\pm}=\mathcal J_0^{-1}\operatorname{ran}W_\pm$. By [F2], this is $\mathcal J_0^{-1}H_{\mathrm{ac}}(C_{\gamma_0})=\mathcal J_0^{-1}H_{\mathrm c}(C_{\gamma_0})$. Positive energy scaling by $c_0$ preserves these spectral subspaces [F3], and the unitary numerical coordinate representation transports the spectral measures and their subspaces as in step 2.1. The resulting physical subspaces are exactly $H_{\mathrm{ac}}(H_\kappa)=H_{\mathrm c}(H_\kappa)$. This proves (b) for every declared reference length, preserving the source's whole continuous subspace and all angular channels. [step 2.1, step 3.1, F2, F3, algebra]

5.1 [Scattering phases, unitarity and free-flow commutation] Put $S^{\mathrm{nd}}=W_+^*W_-$. The formula in step 3.1 gives $S_D=\mathcal J_0^{-1}B_{+,L}^*S^{\mathrm{nd}}B_{-,L}\mathcal J_0.$ All factors are unitary by [F2] and step 2.1, so $S_D$ is unitary. The commutation with the free flow follows directly from the two intertwinings: taking the adjoint of the plus identity at time $-r$ gives $e^{-irA_0}W_+^*=W_+^*e^{-irC_{\gamma_0}}$, hence $S^{\mathrm{nd}}e^{-irA_0}=W_+^*e^{-irC_{\gamma_0}}W_-=e^{-irA_0}S^{\mathrm{nd}}$. The fixed $B_{\pm,L}$ commute with that same flow, so their scattering product does too, and conjugating proves (c). Equivalently the common range projection from step 4.1 gives both $S_D^*S_D=I$ and $S_DS_D^*=I$. For any other reference time $t_\star'$, let $Q_\sigma=q_\sigma(H^{\mathrm{free}})$ with $q_\sigma(E)=\exp(-i\sigma\alpha(E)\log(t_\star'/t_\star))$, $\alpha(E)=m\kappa/(\hbar\sqrt{2mE})$ for $E>0$ and $q_\sigma(0)=1$. The defining phases give exactly $\Omega_{D\pm}'=\Omega_{D\pm}Q_\pm$ and $S_D'=Q_+^*S_DQ_-$. These incoming/outgoing factors are different sign conventions, not a claim that the scattering operator itself is unchanged. [step 2.1, step 3.1, step 4.1, F2, F3, F4, algebra]

6.1 [Scope and assembly] Steps 3.1–5.1 establish all the original modified-limit, isometry, intertwining, full completeness and scattering-unitarity conclusions with their corrected dimensional convention. No step supplies the ordinary unmodified Coulomb wave limits, so (d) retains exactly that distinction. The reference length adds only a comparison convention and its fixed channel phases; it adds no hypothesis on a state or on the Coulomb interaction, no amplitude formula and no measured cross section. [F4, given, step 3.1, step 4.1, step 5.1] ∎

## Statement

Adopt the declared single-channel resonance model
[[def-nrqm-scattering-single-channel-resonance-model]] with channel label $l$,
mass $m>0$, action constant $\hbar>0$ and parameters $E_{r}\in\mathbb R$,
$\Gamma>0$, with the phase shift read modulo $\pi$ from $S_{l}=e^{2i\delta_{l}}$
and the channel cross-section reading $\sigma_{l}(E)$ of that definition.
Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice
([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Put $y:=\Gamma/2>0$.
For every real $E$ define the **auxiliary real-axis Lorentzian factor**
$$L(E):=\frac{y^2}{(E-E_r)^2+y^2}.$$
This is a mathematical extension of the positive-energy phase-shift factor;
physical phase shifts, $k(E)$ and cross sections remain defined only for $E>0$.
Then:

(a) for every $E>0$, $|S_l(E)|=1$ and
$$\delta_l(E)=-\operatorname{Arg}(E-E_r+iy)\quad(\mathrm{modulo}\ \pi),$$
where for $z=x+iy$ with $y>0$, $\operatorname{Arg}z$ is the unique angle
$\theta\in(0,\pi)$ with $\cos\theta=x/\sqrt{x^2+y^2}$ and
$\sin\theta=y/\sqrt{x^2+y^2}$. Equivalently, for $E\ne E_r$ one may use
$\delta_l(E)=-\arctan(y/(E-E_r))$ modulo $\pi$; if $E=E_r>0$,
$\delta_l(E)=-\pi/2$ modulo $\pi$;

(b) for every $E>0$, $\sin^2\delta_l(E)=L(E)$. On the entire real axis,
$L(E)$ has value $1$ exactly at $E=E_r$ and value $1/2$ exactly at
$E=E_r\pm\Gamma/2$. Thus the **full-real-axis half-height width** of this
factor is $\Gamma$ for every real $E_r$. A peak or half-height location is
in the physical energy range only when that location is positive; the
width statement itself concerns $L$ on $\mathbb R$;

(c) for every $E>0$, the channel cross-section reading is
$$\sigma_l(E)=\frac{4\pi}{k(E)^2}(2l+1)L(E),\qquad k(E)=\frac{\sqrt{2mE}}{\hbar},$$
read in $\mathrm{m^2}$. If $E_r>0$, its value at that physical energy is
$$\sigma_l(E_r)=\frac{4\pi\hbar^2}{2mE_r}(2l+1).$$
If $E_r\le0$, this model defines no physical cross section at $E_r$.
No maximum statement at $E_r$ is made for $\sigma_l$ itself, whose energy
dependence also contains the factor $k(E)^{-2}$; no slow-variation
assumption on that factor is required.

Every display is a conditional algebraic statement about the declared model;
no potential producing $S_{l}$, no decay law, no lifetime and no measured
quantity is asserted.

## Example

**Setup.** Adopt the declared single-channel resonance model
[[def-nrqm-scattering-single-channel-resonance-model]] with channel label
$l=0$, mass $m>0$, action constant $\hbar>0$ and parameters $E_{r}>0$,
$\Gamma>0$; read the phase shift and channel cross section by
[[pthm-nrqm-scattering-single-channel-resonance-cross-section]] clauses (a)-(c).
Put $k_r:=k(E_r)=\hbar^{-1}\sqrt{2mE_r}$ and let $L(E)$ on
$\mathbb R$ denote the auxiliary Lorentzian factor of that theorem.

## Example

**Setup.** Adopt the declared single-channel resonance model
[[def-nrqm-scattering-single-channel-resonance-model]] with channel label
$l=0$, mass $m>0$, action constant $\hbar>0$ and parameters $E_{r}>0$,
$\Gamma>0$; read the phase shift and channel cross section by
[[pthm-nrqm-scattering-single-channel-resonance-cross-section]] clauses (a)-(c).
Put $k_r:=k(E_r)=\hbar^{-1}\sqrt{2mE_r}$ and let $L(E)$ on
$\mathbb R$ denote the auxiliary Lorentzian factor of that theorem.

step_quotes.quote: 4.1 On the full real axis, $L$ reaches $1$ at $E_r$ and $1/2$ exactly at $E_r\pm\Gamma/2$, so its full width at half maximum is $\Gamma$. On the positive physical axis both half-height locations are present exactly when $\Gamma<2E_r$; for $\Gamma\ge2E_r$ the lower location is excluded. This qualifies the physical interpretation without narrowing the allowed $E_r>0$, $\Gamma>0$ parameters or changing the real-axis width identity. The example of step 3.1 keeps both half-height points positive and shows that the cross-section ratios there differ from $1/2$. [given, step 1.1, step 2.1, step 3.1, algebra] ∎

2.1 For every physical $E>0$, with $x:=E-E_r$ and $y:=\Gamma/2>0$, dividing by the positive resonance-centre value yields $\sigma_0(E)/\sigma_0(E_r)=(k_r/k(E))^2 y^2/(x^2+y^2)=(E_r/E)L(E)$. At the always-positive upper point the ratio is $E_r/(2(E_r+y))$; at the lower point it is $E_r/(2(E_r-y))$ only when $E_r-y>0$. If that lower point is zero or negative, the real-axis identity $L(E_r-y)=1/2$ is still valid but no physical ratio is evaluated there. The factor $E_r/E$ is energy dependent and need not vary slowly for arbitrary $\Gamma$. [step 1.1, given, algebra]

step_quotes.quote: 3.1 Take the declared parameters $E_{r}=4\,\Gamma$ (both in joules). Then at $E=E_{r}+\Gamma/2=(9/2)\Gamma$ the Lorentzian factor is $1/2$ and the ratio of step 2.1 is $(4/(9/2))(1/2)=4/9$; at $E=(7/2)\Gamma$ the factor is again $1/2$ and the ratio is $(4/(7/2))(1/2)=4/7$. The first value is strictly below $1/2$ and the second strictly above, so this is the explicit asymmetry produced by the $1/E$ factor, so these factor half-height locations are not the locations where $\sigma_0(E)=\sigma_0(E_r)/2$; no maximum of $\sigma_0$ is used in this comparison. [step 2.1, algebra]

## Example

**Setup.** Adopt the declared short-range scattering model
[[def-nrqm-scattering-framework-short-range-model]] with mass $m>0$, spin
zero, action constant $\hbar>0$ and the **uniform ball potential**
$$V(x):=\begin{cases}V_{0},&|x|<R,\\ 0,&|x|>R,\end{cases}\qquad V_{0}\in\mathbb R,\ R>0,$$
read in joules and metres; adopt the stationary beam model at wave number
$k>0$ and direction $d$, and let $W=(2m/\hbar^{2})V$, $q=\|K_{k}\|$, $f_{k}$
and the Born amplitude $f_{B}$ be as in
[[pthm-nrqm-scattering-controlled-born-approximation]]. Write
$\theta$ for the scattering angle, $\cos\theta=\Omega\cdot d$, and
$q_{\mathrm{tr}}:=|k(d-\Omega)|=2k\sin(\theta/2)$ for the momentum transfer.

## Example

**Setup.** Adopt the declared short-range scattering model
[[def-nrqm-scattering-framework-short-range-model]] with mass $m>0$, spin
zero, action constant $\hbar>0$ and the **uniform ball potential**
$$V(x):=\begin{cases}V_{0},&|x|<R,\\ 0,&|x|>R,\end{cases}\qquad V_{0}\in\mathbb R,\ R>0,$$
read in joules and metres; adopt the stationary beam model at wave number
$k>0$ and direction $d$, and let $W=(2m/\hbar^{2})V$, $q=\|K_{k}\|$, $f_{k}$
and the Born amplitude $f_{B}$ be as in
[[pthm-nrqm-scattering-controlled-born-approximation]]. Write
$\theta$ for the scattering angle, $\cos\theta=\Omega\cdot d$, and
$q_{\mathrm{tr}}:=|k(d-\Omega)|=2k\sin(\theta/2)$ for the momentum transfer.

step_quotes.quote: 1.1 By the Born theorem, $f_{B}(\Omega)=-\frac{1}{4\pi}\int_{B_{R}}e^{iq_{\mathrm{tr}}\cdot y}W(y)\,dy$ with $W=V_{0}2m/\hbar^{2}$ constant on $B_{R}$; in polar coordinates the ball integral is $\int_{B_{R}}e^{iq\cdot y}dy=2\pi\int_{0}^{R}\int_{-1}^{1}e^{iqrs}r^{2}\,ds\,dr=4\pi\bigl(\sin(qR)-qR\cos(qR)\bigr)/q^{3}$ for $q=q_{\mathrm{tr}}>0$, and equals $4\pi R^{3}/3$ at $q=0$ by continuity. [given, algebra]

1.2 The kernel $G_{k}(x-y)W(y)$ on $B_{R}\times B_{R}$ has squared Hilbert-Schmidt norm $\int_{B_{R}}\int_{B_{R}}|G_{k}(x-y)W(y)|^{2}dx\,dy=\frac{|V_{0}|^{2}(2m/\hbar^{2})^{2}}{16\pi^{2}}\int_{B_{R}}\int_{B_{R}}|x-y|^{-2}dx\,dy$; for each $y$ the inner integral over $x\in B_{R}$ is at most the integral over the ball of radius $2R$ around $y$, which is $8\pi R$. Hence $\|K_{k}\|\le\|K_{k}\|_{\mathrm{HS}}\le\frac{2m|V_{0}|}{\hbar^{2}}R^{2}\sqrt{2/3}=:q_{\mathrm{HS}}$. [given, algebra]

2.1 Therefore $f_{B}(\Omega)=-\frac{2mV_{0}}{\hbar^{2}}\cdot\frac{\sin(q_{\mathrm{tr}}R)-q_{\mathrm{tr}}R\cos(q_{\mathrm{tr}}R)}{q_{\mathrm{tr}}^{3}}$ for $q_{\mathrm{tr}}>0$, with the forward value $f_{B}(\theta=0)=-\frac{2mV_{0}}{\hbar^{2}}\frac{R^{3}}{3}$; the amplitude has the dimension of length, since $2mV_{0}/\hbar^{2}$ is in $\mathrm{m^{-2}}$ and the bracket in $\mathrm{m^{3}}$. [step 1.1, algebra]

2.2 Consequently, if $\frac{2m|V_{0}|}{\hbar^{2}}R^{2}\sqrt{2/3}<1$, then $q=\|K_{k}\|\le q_{\mathrm{HS}}<1$ and the controlled Born estimate of the theorem applies; since $t\mapsto t/(1-t)$ is increasing on $[0,1)$ and $\|e_{\mathrm{inc}}\|_{L^{2}(B_{R})}=|B_{R}|^{1/2}$, the uniform error bound is at most $|f_{k}(\Omega)-f_{B}(\Omega)|\le\frac{\|W\|_{\infty}|B_{R}|}{4\pi}\frac{q_{\mathrm{HS}}}{1-q_{\mathrm{HS}}}=\frac{2m|V_{0}|}{\hbar^{2}}\frac{R^{3}}{3}\frac{q_{\mathrm{HS}}}{1-q_{\mathrm{HS}}}$ in metres; this is an explicit condition on the declared strength, radius, mass and action constant, verified here without any numerical value of the constants. [step 1.2, given, algebra]

3.1 Under the same condition the beam model reads $d\sigma/d\Omega(0)=|f_{k}(0)|^{2}$, and the theorem controls the difference from $|f_{B}(0)|^{2}$ through the bound of 2.2; the pair asserts the display $|f_{B}(0)|^{2}=\bigl(\frac{2mV_{0}}{\hbar^{2}}\bigr)^{2}\frac{R^{6}}{9}$ as the Born forward reading, read in $\mathrm{m^{2}\,sr^{-1}}$, and no measured value. [step 2.1, step 2.2, given, algebra] ∎

## Example

**Setup.** Adopt the declared short-range scattering model
[[def-nrqm-scattering-framework-short-range-model]] with mass $m>0$, spin
zero, action constant $\hbar>0$, and declare the **Yukawa potential**
$$V_{g,\mu}(x):=-g\,\frac{e^{-\mu|x|}}{|x|}\qquad(x\ne0),\qquad g>0,\ \mu>0,$$
read in joules, with $g$ in $\mathrm{J\,m}$ and $\mu$ in $\mathrm{m^{-1}}$.

## Example

**Setup.** Adopt the declared short-range scattering model
[[def-nrqm-scattering-framework-short-range-model]] with mass $m>0$, spin
zero, action constant $\hbar>0$, and declare the **Yukawa potential**
$$V_{g,\mu}(x):=-g\,\frac{e^{-\mu|x|}}{|x|}\qquad(x\ne0),\qquad g>0,\ \mu>0,$$
read in joules, with $g$ in $\mathrm{J\,m}$ and $\mu$ in $\mathrm{m^{-1}}$.

step_quotes.quote: 1.1 Put $V_{\mathrm{loc}}:=V_{g,\mu}\mathbf 1_{\{|x|<1\}}$ and $V_{\mathrm{tail}}:=V_{g,\mu}\mathbf 1_{\{|x|\ge1\}}$, so that $V_{g,\mu}=V_{\mathrm{loc}}+V_{\mathrm{tail}}$; $V_{\mathrm{loc}}$ is supported in the closed unit ball, and $\int_{\mathbb R^{3}}|V_{\mathrm{loc}}|^{2}dx=4\pi g^{2}\int_{0}^{1}e^{-2\mu r}dr\le4\pi g^{2}<\infty$, so $V_{\mathrm{loc}}\in L^{2}(\mathbb R^{3})$ is compactly supported and $V_{\mathrm{tail}}$ is bounded by $g$. [given, algebra]

## Example

**Setup.** Adopt the declared short-range scattering model
[[def-nrqm-scattering-framework-short-range-model]] with mass $m>0$, spin
zero, action constant $\hbar>0$, and declare the **Yukawa potential**
$$V_{g,\mu}(x):=-g\,\frac{e^{-\mu|x|}}{|x|}\qquad(x\ne0),\qquad g>0,\ \mu>0,$$
read in joules, with $g$ in $\mathrm{J\,m}$ and $\mu$ in $\mathrm{m^{-1}}$.

step_quotes.quote: 1.1 Put $V_{\mathrm{loc}}:=V_{g,\mu}\mathbf 1_{\{|x|<1\}}$ and $V_{\mathrm{tail}}:=V_{g,\mu}\mathbf 1_{\{|x|\ge1\}}$, so that $V_{g,\mu}=V_{\mathrm{loc}}+V_{\mathrm{tail}}$; $V_{\mathrm{loc}}$ is supported in the closed unit ball, and $\int_{\mathbb R^{3}}|V_{\mathrm{loc}}|^{2}dx=4\pi g^{2}\int_{0}^{1}e^{-2\mu r}dr\le4\pi g^{2}<\infty$, so $V_{\mathrm{loc}}\in L^{2}(\mathbb R^{3})$ is compactly supported and $V_{\mathrm{tail}}$ is bounded by $g$. [given, algebra]

2.1 For $|x|\ge1$ one has $|V_{\mathrm{tail}}(x)|=g\,e^{-\mu|x|}/|x|\le g\,e^{-\mu|x|}$, and for every $\delta>0$ the function $r\mapsto e^{-\mu r}(1+r)^{1+\delta}$ is bounded on $[0,\infty)$: on a compact initial interval it is continuous hence bounded, and beyond some $R_{0}$ the estimate $e^{\mu r}\ge C(1+r)^{\delta+1}$ of the cited dominance theorem gives $e^{-\mu r}(1+r)^{1+\delta}\le C^{-1}$; hence with the constant $C_{\delta}:=\sup_{r\ge0}e^{-\mu r}(1+r)^{1+\delta}<\infty$ one has $|V_{\mathrm{tail}}(x)|\le gC_{\delta}(1+|x|)^{-1-\delta}$ for all $|x|\ge1$, and a fortiori almost everywhere on $\mathbb R^{3}$ after adjusting the constant, since the region $|x|<1$ is anyway covered by the local part. [step 1.1, given, algebra]

## Example

**Setup.** Adopt the declared short-range scattering model
[[def-nrqm-scattering-framework-short-range-model]] with mass $m>0$, spin
zero, action constant $\hbar>0$, and declare the **Yukawa potential**
$$V_{g,\mu}(x):=-g\,\frac{e^{-\mu|x|}}{|x|}\qquad(x\ne0),\qquad g>0,\ \mu>0,$$
read in joules, with $g$ in $\mathrm{J\,m}$ and $\mu$ in $\mathrm{m^{-1}}$.

step_quotes.quote: 4.1 As $\mu\to0^{+}$ the potential $V_{g,\mu}$ tends pointwise to $-g/|x|$, the pure Coulomb form with $\kappa=g$; for the limiting potential, and for every split into a compactly supported part and a remainder, the quotient $(1+|x|)^{1+\delta}|V_{\mathrm{tail}}(x)|=g(1+|x|)^{1+\delta}/|x|$ tends to $+\infty$ as $|x|\to\infty$ for every $\delta>0$, so the sufficient decay hypothesis of that theorem fails and the Coulomb case is not covered by the short-range class; its treatment is the separate declared long-range model [[def-nrqm-scattering-coulomb-dollard-model]], for which the theorem supplies no ordinary-comparison statement. [step 2.1, given, algebra] ∎
